title: The Studienkolleg: preparatory courses for university in Germany
description: Who needs a preparatory course, how the courses are organised, what the final exam involves, what it costs and whether English-taught options exist.
html:
Not every school-leaving certificate qualifies for direct admission to a German university. Applicants whose qualification is not considered equivalent to the German Abitur complete a one-year preparatory course, the Studienkolleg, and pass its final exam first. This guide explains who needs it and how it works.

What a Studienkolleg is

A preparatory college attached to a university or run by a federal state, offering two-semester courses that bring international applicants to the level of a German school-leaver in the subjects relevant to their intended degree. It ends with the assessment exam (Feststellungsprüfung), which is the ticket to university admission.

Who needs one

It depends on your country and your certificate. Applicants with an International Baccalaureate, A-levels or a school diploma from an EU country usually qualify directly. Applicants from Pakistan with an HSSC alone usually need either one or two years of university study at home or the preparatory course. The Anabin database and the university's admissions office give the definitive answer for your certificate.

Public and private

Public preparatory colleges charge no tuition, only a semester contribution, but have entrance exams and limited places. Private ones charge fees of several thousand euros a year and admit more flexibly. Both prepare for the same final exam, but check that a private college's exam is recognised by the university you want to attend.

Course types

Courses are grouped by intended degree: a technical course for engineering and science, a medical course for medicine and biology, an economics course, a humanities course and a language-focused course. You choose the course that matches your degree plans, and the assessment exam is only valid for that group of subjects.

Language requirements

Most public preparatory colleges teach in German and require level B1 or B2 at entry; the assessment exam is in German. That means many applicants spend a year on language courses before the preparatory year.

English-taught options

A small number of private colleges offer English-taught preparatory courses that lead to English-taught bachelor's programmes. They are more expensive, but they remove the language year.

Visa and costs

Preparatory course students apply for the same student visa as degree students, with the same proof of funds and health insurance. Budget for living costs of about €1,000 a month plus any tuition, and expect the whole path, language course included, to take two to three years before the degree begins.
